name: token_integration_safety
description: Unsafe ERC-20 integration: raw transfer/approve calls and unchecked transfer amounts for non-standard tokens
question: The source file in `source` contains a contract that calls an ERC-20 token's transfer, transferFrom, or approve function directly (not via SafeERC20 wrappers) or credits an internal balance using the input amount parameter instead of the measured balance difference, such that non-standard tokens (e.g., no bool return, fee-on-transfer, or rebasing tokens) would cause reverted transfers, silent accounting failures, or inflated internal balances.
criteria: Direct call to token.transfer(...), token.transferFrom(...), or token.approve(...) without using SafeERC20's safeTransfer/safeTransferFrom/forceApprove
Approval is set directly to a new non-zero value without first resetting to zero (breaks with USDT-style tokens)
Deposit/transfer-in function increments internal balance or minted shares by the passed 'amount' parameter rather than by measured balanceOf() difference before/after the transfer
No decimals() query is used when computing token amounts, hardcoding 18 decimals for an arbitrary or non-18-decimal token
Contract stores raw token balances for a rebasing token without wrapping it or using share-based accounting
Absence of any SafeERC20 import/usage combined with direct low-level token interface calls
